datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime  @default(now())
  editedAt  DateTime?
  body      String
  article   Article   @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User      @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

content.text:
The spec is written to `specs/feature-3-soft-delete.md`. It names seven rules and gives their source, without copying any values. It is under the 1300-character limit.

**Answers to your three questions**
1. **Deletion and lists:** `policy-soft-delete.md` says deleting sets a timestamp and keeps the row. Deleted comments are left out of comment lists. Only the author may delete.
2. **Error shape and status codes:** `policy-error-response.md` says new errors use an error object with a code and a message. Status codes do not change.
3. **Comment fields:** `code-comment-model.md` lists the fields, but the schema has one more (see disagreements below).

**Disagreements and what I followed**
- **Error shape, note vs. note:** `ops-runbook.md` and `code-error-shape.md` describe the errors-by-field body. `policy-error-response.md` replaces that body. I followed the policy, because it names the older shape as replaced. Support reads the `errors` key, so the runbook needs updating. Please confirm this is the right call.
- **Comment model, note vs. code:** `code-comment-model.md` says there is no `editedAt` field. `app/src/prisma/schema.prisma` has one. The spec relies on the schema, not the note. The note is stale.
- **Ownership, note vs. code:** `code-comment-ownership.md` matches `deleteComment` in `article.service.ts`. Both return 404 for a comment that is missing or belongs to someone else. The 403 branch is unreachable, as the note says.
- **Error handler, code vs. policy:** `main.ts` sends the thrown body as-is. The current handlers use the errors-by-field body. That matches the code today. Changing it is part of the work the policy calls for.

**Planner choices (listed in the spec so you can redirect)**
- The new deletion timestamp is nullable, so existing rows stay live.
- A second delete of a deleted comment returns the same not-found error. The lookup skips deleted comments.
- Existing not-found and forbidden bodies in `deleteComment` keep the old shape, since they are not new errors. This is an open point in the spec.
- Tests go under `app/src/tests/services` with the prisma mock. The release checklist also requires a one-line undo note on the migration.

I did not read `app/src/app/routes/auth/auth.ts`, so the auth-header rule is from the note only. I also did not edit any application code.
